title: LP2 grid as a page-order table?
question: Does the LP2-49–51 256-byte grid contain a contiguous 56- or 57-byte permutation of page indices under its published source bytes or fixed grid readings?
summary: Neither the source 256-byte stream nor 16,384 fixed grid readings contain a contiguous 0–55 or 0–56 page permutation; the longest eligible run is only five bytes.
finding: The pinned source stream has no permutation in its 201 56-byte or 200 57-byte windows. Across 16,384 grid routes and stem readings, zero of 6,569,984 windows pass the necessary value-range condition. The maximum eligible run is three bytes for 0–55 and five for 0–56.
limitations: This checks direct, contiguous unsigned-byte page indices only. It does not exclude a transformed, encrypted or noncontiguous table, different page range, or unread glyph variants beyond the ten registered stems.
next_steps: Any revised page-route claim should specify its transformation, page set and readout before testing, then show a complete route and an independent control.

scope.representation: The source repository’s pinned 256-byte canonical payload plus Liberpedia’s conditional base-60 grid bytes under 16 rectangular routes and 1,024 ten-stem readings.
scope.procedure: Exhaustively scan each 56-byte window for an exact permutation of 0–55 and each 57-byte window for 0–56. Count candidate windows with every byte in range and the longest uninterrupted in-range run.
scope.parameters: 201 and 200 windows per 256-byte stream; 16,384 local streams; 6,569,984 windows total. Two planted positive windows at byte offset 100.
scope.exclusions: Noncontiguous selections, transformed or encrypted values, other page-index sets, more glyph alternatives, alternative bases, and page-order validation beyond a direct table.

review.reviewer: Exhaustive scan and independent run-length check

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; accompanying reference-data bundle and pinned 256-byte source included with experiment.

visuals.caption: The longest run of eligible byte values is far shorter than a literal 56/57-page permutation needs.

reader_note: No contiguous 56/57-page index permutation occurs in 6.57 million direct windows.
reader_limit: Only literal contiguous page-index bytes under specified readings are excluded.
